status: frozen before implementation and before observing any population-density-control result
motivation: At fixed 5,023 slots, released queries cover unsupported regions by transporting points away from FLAME-supported detail. A 2x density control tests whether the observed coverage-sharpness frontier is a finite allocation effect or a more intrinsic release penalty.

intervention.new_condition: 10,046 slots: all original FLAME vertices plus 5,023 deterministic topology-consistent barycentric surface samples
intervention.semantic_consistency: The same face indices and barycentric coordinates are used for every identity; original vertices remain the first nested 5,023 slots.
intervention.smoothness_graph: Original mesh edges plus edges from every added surface sample to its three parent triangle vertices.
intervention.region_assignment: Added samples inherit each region only when at least two parent triangle vertices belong to that FLAME mask region.
intervention.parameter_matching: hard, adaptive, and released are parameter-matched within 2x density. The 2x model intentionally has more slot embeddings than the 1x anchor; this is a representation-density intervention, not an equal-total-parameter capacity test.
unchanged: NeRSemble identity splits and held-out cameras

primary_outcomes: released-minus-hard head-supported PSNR and LPIPS at N_obs=4
released-minus-hard head-unsupported PSNR and LPIPS at N_obs=4
change in the N_id=384 minus N_id=8 released advantage

predictions.finite_allocation_supported: At 2x density, released head-supported PSNR/LPIPS loss shrinks relative to 1x while released head-unsupported gain remains positive.
predictions.support_ceiling_supported: Hard 2x gains less from identity scaling on head-unsupported content than released 2x and does not erase the released advantage.
predictions.crossover_shift: More slots move the head-foreground crossover toward fewer identities or increase the released advantage at N_id=8.

falsifiers: If 2x density leaves the released supported-detail penalty unchanged, simple point-budget dilution is not a sufficient mechanism.
If hard 2x eliminates the head-unsupported released advantage, the 1x ceiling was primarily sampling density rather than FLAME support.
If both hard and released improve equally and their scaling interaction is unchanged, density is orthogonal to the identified phase boundary at this range.
paired_inference: Average target cameras and training seeds within each held-out identity, then perform a 10,000-sample identity bootstrap.
disclosure: Designed after the 1x primary result and reported as a post-primary mechanism control.
